claims.summary: For every pair of 32-bit inputs, the gcd export returns their unsigned greatest common divisor as a 32-bit value.
claims.statement:
∀ (a b : BitVec 32),
  FVA.Wasm.Exec.Returns Examples.Rust.Lifted.module "gcd" [FVA.Wasm.Exec.Val.i32 a, FVA.Wasm.Exec.Val.i32 b]
    [FVA.Wasm.Exec.Val.i32 (BitVec.ofNat 32 (a.toNat.gcd b.toNat))]
claims.reason: The statement specifies the unsigned greatest common divisor for every 32-bit input pair, including gcd(a, 0) = a, as intended.
claims.name: Examples.Rust.gcd
claims.intent: `gcd(a, b)` on unsigned 32-bit ints: their greatest common divisor (`gcd(a, 0) = a`).
details: Covers every pair of 32-bit inputs, interpreted as unsigned values for the gcd calculation.
The result is the greatest common divisor of those unsigned values, encoded as a 32-bit result.
Returns guarantees a fresh instance exists and, under every host behavior, the call terminates without a trap and returns exactly the specified value.
caveats: The claim describes unsigned mathematical gcd of the two 32-bit bit patterns, not signed integer gcd; conversion back to 32 bits wraps modulo 2^32 (though the gcd itself fits).
It does not specify memory effects or any behavior for exports other than this call.

claims.summary: For every triple of 32-bit inputs, the clamp export returns the first input bounded by the second and third according to signed comparison, in the specified comparison order.
claims.statement:
∀ (x lo hi : BitVec 32),
  FVA.Wasm.Exec.Returns Examples.Rust.Lifted.module "clamp"
    [FVA.Wasm.Exec.Val.i32 x, FVA.Wasm.Exec.Val.i32 lo, FVA.Wasm.Exec.Val.i32 hi]
    [FVA.Wasm.Exec.Val.i32 (if x.slt lo = true then lo else if hi.slt x = true then hi else x)]
claims.reason: The statement implements the stated signed clamp comparison order for every 32-bit triple, including when lo exceeds hi.
claims.name: Examples.Rust.clamp
claims.intent: `clamp(x, lo, hi)` on signed 32-bit ints: `lo` below `lo`, `hi` above `hi`, else `x`.
details: Covers every triple of 32-bit inputs, interpreting comparisons as signed two’s-complement comparisons.
If x is below lo, the result is lo; otherwise, if hi is below x, it is hi; otherwise, it is x. The selected input bit pattern is returned unchanged.
There is no arithmetic here, so no arithmetic wraparound occurs.
Returns guarantees a fresh instance exists and, under every host behavior, the call terminates without a trap and returns exactly the specified value.
caveats: The bounds are not required to be ordered; the expression checks the lower bound first, then the upper bound, so reversed bounds still have a defined result.
The claim is only about the returned value; it does not state anything about memory or other exports.
